families.rationale: Post-earnings-announcement drift continues in the direction of the earnings surprise and fades with the age of the report.
Post-earnings-announcement drift continues in the direction of the announcement-window reaction and fades with the age of the report.

Reaction-direction drift is confined to roughly one holding horizon (20 sessions) after the report. The score divides by the 0/1 window condition, so a name outside the window has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among in-window names only.

Drift is strongest when the surprise and the reaction agree (the PEAD leg rule), within one holding horizon of the report. The score divides by the 0/1 window condition, so a name outside the window has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among in-window names only.
Drift scales with the joint magnitude of the surprise and the reaction and fades with the age of the report.

Price momentum measured outside the announcement window continues (Jegadeesh and Titman, 1993). The score divides by the 0/1 condition, so a name within 20 sessions of a report has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among quiet names only.

Short-term reversal measured outside the announcement window (Jegadeesh, 1990; Lehmann, 1990). The score divides by the 0/1 condition, so a name within 20 sessions of a report has no score (NaN, ineligible) and the decile is taken among quiet names only.
Trailing dividend yield is a cross-sectional return factor (dividend-yield premium).

rationale: A predeclared fixed set of eight event-conditioned formulas, one per family, each scored once without search on daily bars read at D-1 together with the four dimensionless events_fields_v1 columns (earnings_age, earnings_surprise, earnings_reaction, dividend_yield), so search-power check B does not apply; checks A and C still bind. Every field holds state known at the prior close under the PEAD visibility convention: a report dated D completes when D+1 closes and is first visible on row D+1, so the first decision session that can use it is D+2. No field looks forward. A name change that moves a ticker onto or off a cohort symbol is an identity break: that symbol's fields are NaN before its latest break and earlier calendar and corporate-action rows are dropped. Each dividend is scaled by f, the adjusted/raw close ratio at its ex-date, before the trailing-252-session sum and divided by the adjusted close at T. The four windowed formulas divide by their 0/1 window condition, so an out-of-window name has no score (NaN, ineligible) and each session's decile is taken among in-window names only, never completed by tiebreak. The inputs are the digest-pinned offline Nasdaq calendar page cache and the cohort-v2 corporate-actions acquisition. The cohort, label cube, windows, selection, gates, bootstrap, power and null-check parameters are campaign v4's and intraday-v1's, so the cached cube is reused and the lane-wide confirmation window remains unused until a finalist freezes; realized-volatility operators stay forbidden.
title: Events pooled campaign v1: cohort v2, daily bars read at D-1 plus the four events_fields_v1 event fields, predeclared fixed set of eight event-conditioned formulas (checks A and C), one-shot lane-wide confirmation
